content.text:
I fixed it in `lib/adapters/http.js`. I haven't run any tests or tried the reproduction from the issue.

**Cause:** axios defaults `maxBodyLength` to `-1`, meaning unlimited. But it only passed the value on to `follow-redirects` when it was greater than `-1`. So whenever redirects were enabled (the default), `follow-redirects` fell back to its own 10MB limit. With `maxRedirects: 0`, plain `http`/`https` is used instead, which has no limit, so the behaviour changed depending on `maxRedirects`.

**Fix:** when `maxBodyLength` is `-1` (or not set), axios now passes `Infinity` to `follow-redirects`. A body has no size limit by default, whatever `maxRedirects` is set to, and `maxBodyLength: -1` now means unlimited as intended.

I didn't touch the README or changelog. The README already describes `maxBodyLength` as an optional limit, which matches the behaviour now.
